translation: הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר הָיָה אֶל יִרְמְיָהוּ, אֶל כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים הַיֹּשְׁבִים בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם — הַיֹּשְׁבִים בְּמִגְדֹּל וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵס וּבְנֹף וּבְאֶרֶץ פַּתְרוֹס — לֵאמֹר:

tokens.notes: Lemma: דָּבָר (dāḇār). The root דָּבַר means to speak, arrange, or command. As a noun, it encompasses speech, matter, and purpose—anything ‘spoken’ into existence. Here, it marks the initiation of a formal prophetic oracle.
Relative pronoun. Links the noun to the following relative clause.
Lemma: הָיָה (hāyāh). To be, become, come to pass. In prophetic literature, this often carries the weight of actualization—the word doesn’t just exist; it ‘happens’ or ‘arrives’ to the prophet.
tokens.grammar: Verb, qal perfect, 3rd person masculine singular.

tokens.notes: Preposition denoting motion towards or direction. Indicates the word ‘came to’ or ‘was directed to’ the prophet.
Proper name. Meaning relates to ‘YHWH lifts up’ or ‘YHWH establishes.’
Preposition, repeated for emphasis and clarity, specifying the secondary audience of the oracle.
Noun meaning totality. Emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the oracle’s audience.
Gentilic name. Refers to the people of Judah, the Jews. This term becomes increasingly common in exilic and post-exilic texts.
tokens.grammar: Adjective used as a substantive, masculine plural, definite.

tokens.notes: From יָשַׁב (yāšaḇ), to sit, remain, dwell. The participle here specifies those who are settled or residing in a location.
tokens.grammar: Verb, qal active participle, masculine plural, definite.

tokens.notes: Preposition בְּ + noun אֶרֶץ (’ereṣ). The noun means land, earth, or territory.
Proper noun. The dual form originally denoted Upper and Lower Egypt.
Participle repeated. The repetition narrows the general description to specific locations.
tokens.grammar: Verb, qal active participle, masculine plural, definite.

tokens.notes: Preposition בְּ + proper noun מִגְדֹּל (Miḡdōl). A fortress or tower; here, a specific location in Egypt, likely near the eastern border.
Conjunction + Preposition + proper noun. תַּחְפַּנְחֵס (Taḥpanḥēs) is identified with the Egyptian city of Daphnae, a frontier fortress.
Conjunction + Preposition + proper noun. נֹף (Nōp) is the Hebrew name for Memphis, the ancient capital of Egypt.
Conjunction + Preposition + noun. The list concludes with a broader regional designation.
Proper noun. Refers to Upper Egypt (Pathros). The association is further elaborated in Isaiah 11:11.
tokens.grammar: Proper noun, masculine (used as geographical name).

tokens.notes: Infinitive construct from אָמַר (’āmar). Marks the beginning of direct discourse, setting up the quote to follow.
